quests.scene: An employer offers you a salary that is below your expectations during a negotiation.
options: I expected more - raise it immediately.
Thank you for the offer. Based on my experience and market research I was hoping for something closer to my target figure. Is there flexibility?
Fine I'll take it.
I resign.
quests.hint: Open with gratitude then state your position with clear reasoning.
quests.explanation: Thanking them before countering is confident and professional.

quests.scene: A respected colleague publicly disagrees with your proposal in a team meeting.
options: You are wrong and I'll prove it.
I see your point. Perhaps we could discuss this further after the meeting?
Fine - we'll do everything your way.
Why are you doing this to me?
quests.hint: Acknowledge their view and de-escalate without backing down entirely.
quests.explanation: I see your point - could we discuss this after the meeting? preserves the relationship and avoids public conflict.

quests.scene: You accidentally overhear confidential company information that you were not meant to hear.
options: Share it immediately with your team.
Tell your manager what happened and ask how to proceed.
Forget you heard it and say nothing.
Use it to your advantage discreetly.
quests.hint: Transparency with your manager is the only ethical path here.
quests.explanation: Telling your manager you accidentally heard something confidential is transparent and ethical.

quests.scene: Someone interrupts you mid-sentence in an important meeting.
options: Stop talking and let them speak.
Raise your voice to continue speaking over them.
Say calmly: Sorry - could I just finish my point?
Give them a sharp look.
quests.hint: Politely reclaim your speaking time without aggression.
quests.explanation: Sorry - could I just finish my point? is politely assertive.

quests.scene: A client requests a discount that is well beyond your company's standard policy.
options: I can offer you our loyalty discount - ten percent on your next order. That is the most I'm authorised to offer.
No that is absolutely impossible.
All right I'll make an exception this once.
Let me ask my manager while you sit here waiting.
quests.hint: Offer what you can and be clear and honest about your limits.
quests.explanation: Offering the maximum within your authority is honest helpful and professional.

quests.scene: A colleague asks your honest opinion about their new business idea and you have serious reservations.
options: It sounds absolutely amazing!
Honestly it's not very good at all.
I think there's something interesting here. I do have a few concerns - would you like to hear them?
I need more time to think about it.
quests.hint: Lead with something genuine and offer critique as support not judgment.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging potential while offering to share concerns keeps the conversation collaborative.

quests.scene: You are presenting a project and someone asks a technical question you cannot answer.
options: Make something up quickly so you don't look bad.
That's a great question. I don't have that data with me right now - I'll find out and get back to you.
Why are you asking that?
Skip the question and move on.
quests.hint: Admitting you don't know and promising to follow up is more credible than guessing.
quests.explanation: Saying I don't have that data right now - I'll get back to you shows intellectual honesty.

quests.scene: A new client keeps calling you outside of your normal working hours.
options: Ignore all calls received outside working hours.
Answer at any hour to keep the client happy.
At your next interaction say: To give you the best support could we agree to keep calls within business hours?
Block their number immediately.
quests.hint: Set professional boundaries in a way that frames them as being in the client's interest.
quests.explanation: Framing the boundary as being about service quality is a professional and non-confrontational way to establish working hour expectations.

quests.scene: Your team misses an important deadline because of poor planning. Your manager asks what went wrong.
options: It wasn't my fault at all.
Blame the team member who caused the delay.
I take responsibility - we underestimated the timeline. Here is what we learned and how we will prevent this in future.
We simply had too much work.
quests.hint: Leaders accept responsibility and immediately offer solutions and learning.
quests.explanation: Accepting responsibility naming the lesson and presenting a concrete plan shows genuine leadership maturity.

quests.scene: You are asked to do something at work that conflicts with your personal values.
options: Just do it - it's only work.
I am afraid this isn't something I can do in good conscience. Could I speak with you privately about this?
Quit on the spot immediately.
Do it but complain loudly afterward.
quests.hint: Raise ethical concerns privately and calmly through the right channels.
quests.explanation: Asking to speak privately shows you take the issue seriously without creating a public incident.

quests.scene: A customer becomes verbally aggressive toward you on the phone.
options: Shout back at them.
Hang up immediately.
I understand you're frustrated but we both need to be respectful to resolve this. Can we continue on that basis?
Apologise profusely for everything.
quests.hint: Acknowledge the emotion set a clear standard and keep the door open.
quests.explanation: Validating the frustration setting a clear expectation and giving them the choice to continue is how professionals handle difficult customers.

quests.scene: You immediately forget someone's name right after being formally introduced.
options: Avoid using their name for the rest of the event.
I'm so sorry - I didn't quite catch your name?
Call them you throughout the evening.
Quietly ask someone else nearby.
quests.hint: Asking again immediately is far more gracious than avoiding the name all night.
quests.explanation: I'm so sorry - I didn't quite catch your name? is natural and polite.

quests.scene: You need to exit a long and boring conversation at a networking event.
options: Just walk away without warning.
This has been lovely - I want to let you mingle. Thank you so much for the conversation!
Look at your phone to signal you want to leave.
Tell them honestly that you are bored.
quests.hint: Exit graciously while making the other person feel good about the interaction.
quests.explanation: This exit validates the conversation and frames leaving as giving them the freedom to network.

quests.scene: A team member consistently contributes far less than everyone else on the team.
options: Complain to your manager without speaking to them first.
Just do their work for them to keep the project moving.
Say privately: I've noticed you seem less engaged lately. Is everything OK? I want us to work well as a team.
Ignore it and let it continue.
quests.hint: Address the behaviour directly and privately before considering escalation.
quests.explanation: Checking in first treats the colleague as a person not just a problem.

quests.scene: You realize mid-project that you have fundamentally misunderstood the brief.
options: Finish it incorrectly and hope no one notices.
Start completely over without telling the client anything.
Contact the client immediately: I want to flag a concern about scope - could we have a quick call to clarify?
Blame the original brief.
quests.hint: Flag problems early - early discovery of a misunderstanding is far easier to fix.
quests.explanation: Raising the concern promptly and asking for a clarifying call is professional.

quests.scene: You are interviewing a job candidate who is clearly very nervous. How do you open?
options: Let's begin. First question.
Don't worry about the nerves - let's just have a good conversation.
You seem nervous. Are you all right?
We have thirty minutes. Let's not waste any of it.
quests.hint: Put a nervous candidate at ease without drawing too much attention to the nerves.
quests.explanation: Let's just have a conversation reframes the interview as dialogue rather than examination.

quests.scene: You need to decline an invitation to an optional work social event.
options: I'll definitely be there!
I'm afraid I have a prior commitment that evening but thank you for the invitation.
I'm not going to that kind of thing.
Work events are not really for me.
quests.hint: Decline graciously with a brief and courteous reason.
quests.explanation: A polite decline with a brief reason is socially smooth and professional.

quests.scene: A client tells you: I feel like I'm not getting enough value from this service.
options: That's not a fair assessment at all.
I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me more about what's missing? I want to make sure we get this right.
We provide excellent value to all our clients.
Other clients are very satisfied.
quests.hint: Treat a value concern as an invitation to understand and genuinely improve.
quests.explanation: Apologising asking clarifying questions and expressing commitment shows you take their concern seriously.

quests.scene: You are at a networking dinner and are seated next to someone you do not know at all.
options: Look at your phone and wait for them to speak first.
Ask immediately: What do you do?
Hi I'm [name]. Have you been to one of these events before?
Eat silently and wait for the meal to end.
quests.hint: Break the ice with a warm introduction and an easy low-pressure opening question.
quests.explanation: Introducing yourself and asking a light easy question is natural and low-pressure.

quests.scene: You receive a work email - copied to everyone on the team - that unfairly criticises your work.
options: Reply to all immediately with your full defence.
Reply only to the sender and request a private meeting.
Forward it directly to HR.
Ignore it and carry on.
quests.hint: Keep sensitive professional disagreements private - never escalate in a group email.
quests.explanation: Replying only to the sender prevents escalation and allows for a proper conversation.

quests.scene: You have been asked to mentor a junior colleague who seems resistant to any advice.
options: Give up - they clearly don't want help.
Impose your preferred approach on them regardless.
Ask: What kind of support would actually be most useful to you right now?
Report their resistance to management.
quests.hint: Ask what the mentee needs instead of assuming you know.
quests.explanation: Asking what kind of support they want shifts the dynamic to collaborative partnership.

quests.scene: You are running fifteen minutes late for an important meeting. What do you do?
options: Arrive late and apologise when you get there.
Text immediately: Running 15 mins late - so sorry. Please start without me.
Send a vague message: on my way.
Cancel the entire meeting.
quests.hint: Give a specific honest and considerate advance warning.
quests.explanation: A timely specific message with an apology and permission to start respects everyone's time.

quests.scene: A colleague shares wonderful personal news - they are expecting their first baby.
options: Is it planned?
Congratulations! That's absolutely wonderful news!
Are you planning to take a long maternity leave?
Nod politely and return to your work.
quests.hint: Respond to significant personal news with genuine and appropriate warmth.
quests.explanation: Congratulations! That's absolutely wonderful news! is the appropriate warm response.

quests.scene: You are about to leave a company and want to maintain your relationship with your manager.
options: Never contact them again once you leave.
Add them instantly to every social media platform.
Send a thoughtful thank-you note recognising their specific support and mentorship.
Leave quietly without saying a proper goodbye.
quests.hint: A genuine farewell creates a lasting positive professional impression.
quests.explanation: A sincere thank-you note upon leaving a company is gracious and professional.

quests.scene: You are about to enter a salary negotiation. What is the ideal mindset to bring?
options: Win at all costs no matter what.
Confident but open to finding a genuinely good outcome for both sides.
Be prepared to give everything away to reach agreement.
Let the other side lead and react to everything they say.
quests.hint: Good negotiators seek mutual benefit not just their own win.
quests.explanation: Entering a negotiation with confidence combined with openness to collaboration produces better more durable agreements.

quests.scene: A former colleague asks you to write them a reference but you found them genuinely difficult to work with.
options: Write a glowing reference - be a good friend.
Decline and explain you're not the right person to reference them well.
Write a critical reference.
Let the call ring out and hope they forget.
quests.hint: It is better to decline honestly than to provide an inaccurate reference.
quests.explanation: If you cannot provide a strong honest reference declining and suggesting someone better placed is the ethical choice.

quests.scene: A customer directly asks you what you think of a competitor's product.
options: Their product is honestly terrible.
I can't really compare directly but I can tell you exactly what makes our product the right choice for your specific needs.
I genuinely have no opinion on them.
Buy ours not theirs - obviously.
quests.hint: Stay professional and focus on your product's genuine strengths not competitors' weaknesses.
quests.explanation: Avoiding direct criticism of competitors and refocusing on your own product's value is professional and effective.

quests.scene: You find a significant error in a report just before it is sent to a senior board.
options: Let it go - it's probably not critical.
Correct it and inform the responsible person about what you found.
Tell the board directly without speaking to the author first.
Delete the report.
quests.hint: Fix the error and communicate with the right person - in that order.
quests.explanation: Correcting the error and telling the responsible person is the right sequence.

quests.scene: A colleague vents to you about another team member. You are friendly with both people.
options: Agree with everything they say to be supportive.
Share what you know about the other person from private conversations.
Listen validate their feelings but avoid taking sides or sharing information.
Immediately tell the other colleague what was said.
quests.hint: Be a supportive listener without becoming a messenger or taking sides.
quests.explanation: Listening and validating feelings without sharing information is the diplomatically safe and emotionally intelligent response.

quests.scene: An interviewer asks: Where do you see yourself in five years?
options: In your job if all goes well.
Honestly I haven't really thought about it very much.
I'm looking to grow into a leadership role in this field and I believe this company is the right environment to build that path.
Retired hopefully!
quests.hint: Show genuine ambition and connect it to this specific company.
quests.explanation: Expressing a desire for leadership growth and connecting it to the company shows both genuine ambition and specific interest.
